REAL — discover 2026-08-22, and the most valuable of the new channels. Leviton name 'Heat Pump', LB240-0ST, 40 A 2-pole; blackstart B-10-12 is the Bryant 284ANV060000 5-ton variable-speed outdoor unit on slots 10/12 at 40 A. Installed 2026-08-22 (breaker object created 16:10Z) as part of taking the panel almost fully smart; the collector picked it up on its next hourly hierarchy refresh with no restart and no code change. Leviton's branchType is 'Air Conditioner' and, like the CT usageType, THAT IS A DROPDOWN SOMEBODY PICKED, not a fact: this unit is a heat pump and carries both cooling and heating. Observed 683 W + 667 W = 1,350 W with the compressor at part capacity. Two consequences. (1) It closes the gap blackstart's load meter warns about — B-10-12 was the last device with no traced load, so the Panel B meter reads LOW by exactly this circuit; a few days of history here is what lets a real figure replace the 0 W. (2) It is the instantaneous counterpart to the bryant 'cooling' and 'hpheat' daily-energy channels, which are the SAME physical unit reported by a second cloud at day grain. Correlate them, never sum them. This channel — not leviton ct_2_a/ct_2_b, which are on the strip-heat feeder — is the one that tracks cooling. `category` is spelled out as 'hvac' here, overriding the 'appliance_240v' that blackstart's circuitType would supply, and it is load-bearing rather than cosmetic: /ui/hvac selects the panel side of its Bryant comparison by exactly this category, so a future HVAC circuit reaches that screen by being mapped, not by a code change. mappings.label: HVAC subpanel feeder (leg A) — electric strip heat
mappings.notes: REAL — discover 2026-08-17. Leviton reports usageType HEAT_PUMP on this clamp pair, and THAT LABEL IS NOT AUTHORITATIVE — it is a dropdown someone picked in the app, which is why the label is overridden here (PLAN.md §9's explicit-override rule). What the clamps are physically on is the feeder to the HVAC subpanel, which blackstart B-6-8 describes as 'Feed-through lug tap — feeds the HVAC subpanel'; that subpanel holds the KFCEH3301C20 20 kW heat kit, i.e. the ELECTRIC STRIPS, not the compressor. The 5-ton Bryant 284ANV060000 outdoor unit is a separate circuit (blackstart B-10-12) and is not metered by this pair. Evidence: observed a flat 0 W across 17 minutes of continuous cooling with the blower running and the compressor at 35% capacity — the compressor's power was demonstrably not passing through these clamps. UNVERIFIED: the subpanel has not been opened, so this is a strong inference from the inventory plus the observed behaviour, not confirmed wiring. Expect this channel to read ~0 all summer and to carry real load only during defrost, aux heat and deep winter. breaker_p10 on this hub (the compressor) is the channel to correlate with cooling, NOT this one — and as of 2026-08-22 it exists: an LB240-0ST smart breaker was installed on B-10-12, so the strip-heat inference below can now be tested against a real compressor series instead of resting on the observed flat 0 W. INDEPENDENT CORROBORATION 2026-08-22: the Leviton app's own placeholder object at Panel B position 6 — the two positions the feed-through lug occupies — is named 'Heat Strip Subpanel' by the owner. That is a second, separately recorded statement that 6/8 feeds the HVAC subpanel, which is what this clamp pair is on.
